chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Recite the Verse of the Throne, and get cupping done on whichever day you wish, and give charity, and go out on whichever day you wish.

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: The Verse of the Throne (Quran 2:255), known for its protective virtues.
key_terms.احْتَجِمْ: Get cupping done; a prophetic medical practice involving suction cups.
key_terms.اخْرُجْ: Go out; depart or travel, often implying leaving one's home or city.
key_terms.تَصَدَّقْ: Give charity; voluntary almsgiving for spiritual merit.

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended acts for protection and well-being according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the flexibility in timing ('whichever day you wish') highlights the ease and accessibility of these acts, encouraging consistent spiritual and physical maintenance without rigid constraints. The inclusion of Hijamah alongside Ayat al-Kursi reflects the Shia tradition of integrating prophetic medicine with Quranic recitation for holistic well-being, while the mention of 'exiting' (Khuruj) may allude to general travel or pilgrimage, underscoring the importance of movement and charity in sustaining faith. This concise directive serves as a practical guide for daily devotion, emphasizing that spiritual merit is not bound by specific dates but by sincere intention and regular practice.
